truths.truth: A prose-agreement test pins BOTH halves of D-04 and fails when either is reverted
truths.evidence: cadence-core/bin/prose-agreement.test.mjs:707 reads execute.md's locate step by its own <step name="locate"> anchor. Falsification on a scratch COPY of cadence-core+skills (repo untouched): baseline pass; deleting the `- DERIVED status ...` bullet -> FAIL ('names no /cad-undo route'); rewriting the status bullet to 'If `$ARGUMENTS` is empty, else run' -> FAIL ('runs planning.mjs status conditionally'); removing `complete` from both trigger and rationale -> FAIL ('does not name derived status `complete`'); restored -> pass. Caveat recorded as a minor gap: narrowing only the TRIGGER to `executed` while leaving the rationale sentence that mentions `complete` stays GREEN (observed).

truths.truth: The locate step's refusal exists, is on the DERIVED status, names the supported path and --rerun, and sits before git_guard / the phase_start anchor / any dispatch
truths.evidence: cadence-core/workflows/execute.md:26-36 (the refusal arm) inside <step name="locate"> at :8; <step name="git_guard"> starts at :58 and holds the `trace append --event phase_start` at :109, so the refusal is upstream of both. The status call at :10-13 is stated 'ALWAYS run ... Unconditionally, never under an "else"'. Wired: skills/cad-execute/SKILL.md @-includes cadence-core/workflows/execute.md as its <execution_context>, and its argument-hint reads "[phase number] [--rerun]"; `--rerun` occurs only at execute.md:21,26,30, skills/cad-execute/SKILL.md:4 and the test - no orphan flag elsewhere.

truths.evidence: No runnable probe: every artifact on this path is prose an agent executes (execute.md's locate step). Static placement is verified in truth 4; the firing is not observable without a live slash-command run.

truths.truth: self-verify is clean and the weight budgets the prose edits forced were re-pinned in the same commit as each prose edit
truths.evidence: `node cadence-core/bin/self-verify.mjs --root .` -> {"ok":true,...,"problems":[]} (25 checks). Same-commit re-pins observed in git: 4f644d7 (execute.md 27834->28097), 0106ba8 (worktree-executor.md 3038->3441), 48361c6 (cad-executor-contract 12050->12458), b93522b (execute.md 28097->29218 and cad-execute 742->752), each alongside its prose file and nothing else. `node cadence-core/bin/weight.mjs --root .` measures execute.md 29215 vs 29218, worktree-executor.md 3441 vs 3441, cad-executor-contract 12458 vs 12458, cad-execute 752 vs 752 - all at or under budget (the 3-byte slack is the gate commit b3e5ded shrinking execute.md, which cannot overrun).

truths.truth: On a SUMMARY-less phase, the glob workflows/report.md uses resolves to BOTH the rotated and the current report, and the rotated bytes are unchanged
truths.evidence: Named test 'AC6: both names rotation produces are matched by /cad-report's own glob' passes: it builds phases/1/reports with no SUMMARY.md, rotates by the module, and globSync('phases/1/reports/plan-*.md') resolves ['plan-1.1.md','plan-1.md'] with the rotated Buffer equal to pre-rotation. Falsified on the scratch COPY by making the module answer `run-<n>/plan-<k>.md`: that case FAILS with '- plan-1.1.md' missing from the resolved set. cadence-core/workflows/report.md:66 still carries the unchanged '.planning/phases/<N>/reports/plan-*.md ONLY when SUMMARY is absent' rule.

truths.truth: The phase docs commit transport carries a rotated report into history and keeps the flagged .diff out
truths.evidence: execute.md:471-481 stages the `<plandir>/reports/` DIRECTORY with `git add <plandir>/reports/ ':(exclude)<plandir>/reports/*.diff'`. Behavioral probe in a throwaway git repo (scratchpad/transports, git 2.55.0): after mv plan-1.md -> plan-1.1.md plus a new plan-1.md and a plan-1-risk-task-2.diff, that exact command staged 'A plan-1.1.md / M plan-1.md', the commit put 'RUN A' at plan-1.1.md in history, and the .diff stayed untracked.

truths.truth: A worktree executor's report commit actually carries the rotated report onto the branch
truths.evidence: cadence-core/references/worktree-executor.md:22-28 states the transport as `git commit -- <plandir>/reports/plan-<k>.md [<plandir>/reports/plan-<k>.<n>.md]` with no staging step (no `git add` appears anywhere in that file for the report, and skills/cad-executor-contract/SKILL.md mentions `git add` only at :82 as a prohibition). Probe in a throwaway git repo (git 2.55.0): the rotated path is a NEW untracked path, and `git commit -m r2 -- reports/plan-1.md reports/plan-1.1.md` exits 1 with "error: pathspec 'reports/plan-1.1.md' did not match any file(s) known to git" - nothing is committed, so the widening loses BOTH reports where the old by-name form would at least have committed the current one. Staging the two report paths first and then running the same pathspec commit works (exit 0, both files in the commit) and still leaves the risk_surface change staged and uncommitted and the .diff untracked, so the guardrail the bullet protects survives the fix.

truths.truth: A live executor rotates the previous run's report before its first write, so two real runs of one plan leave two readable records
truths.evidence: The rule is prose only - skills/cad-executor-contract/SKILL.md:203-209 states rotate-before-first-write and cites cadence-core/bin/lib/report-rotation.mjs (cited, never invoked: `grep -n 'node .*report-rotation'` finds nothing, and no CONTRACTS row exists, matching self-verify check 14). agents/cad-executor.md preloads that skill, so the rule reaches the executor; nothing in the tree imports the module at runtime, so the rename itself is only ever performed by an agent and no probe observes it.

gaps.name: Rotated report survives the commit transports
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - the worktree half of the transport cannot execute. `git commit -- <paths>` refuses a path git does not track, and a rotated report is always a brand-new untracked path, so the widened pathspec aborts the whole commit instead of carrying the rotated file.
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/references/worktree-executor.md:22-28 documents `git commit -- <plandir>/reports/plan-<k>.md [<plandir>/reports/plan-<k>.<n>.md]` with no staging step; that file contains no `git add` for the report and skills/cad-executor-contract/SKILL.md names `git add` only at :82 to forbid `-A`/`.`. Probe (git 2.55.0, throwaway repo): with plan-1.md tracked, `mv` to plan-1.1.md, new plan-1.md written, `git commit -m r2 -- reports/plan-1.md reports/plan-1.1.md` -> exit 1, "error: pathspec 'reports/plan-1.1.md' did not match any file(s) known to git", zero commits. The same probe with `git add reports/plan-1.md reports/plan-1.1.md` first -> exit 0, both files in the commit, the risk_surface change still staged and uncommitted, the .diff still untracked. (The docs-commit half of this item is fine: `git add <plandir>/reports/ ':(exclude)...*.diff'` was probed and does carry the rotated file into history.)
gaps.missing: In cadence-core/references/worktree-executor.md's commit-the-report bullet, stage the named report paths before the pathspec commit (`git add <plandir>/reports/plan-<k>.md [<plandir>/reports/plan-<k>.<n>.md]` then the same `git commit --` pathspec), and say why the add is bounded to those paths rather than a `git add` of the directory - the flagged .diff lives there and a bare `git commit` after a broad add is what the bullet already forbids. Note the same untracked-path failure pre-exists for a FIRST run's report (probe case A: `git commit -- reports/plan-1.md` on an untracked report also exits 1), so the fix closes both. The file measures 3441 against a 3441 budget, so re-pin cadence-core/bin/weight-budgets.json's worktree-executor.md row in the same commit or self-verify goes budget-overrun.

gaps.name: The prose-agreement test stays green when the refusal is narrowed to `executed` alone
gaps.reason: behavior wrong (weak assertion) - the test's own comment claims it catches 'a later edit [that] can narrow [the refusal] to `executed` alone', but it only greps the arm for the literal `complete`, which the arm's explanatory sentence supplies independently of the trigger.
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/prose-agreement.test.mjs:742-746 asserts `refusal` matches /`complete`/ anywhere in the bullet. Probe on the scratch copy: changing the trigger to 'DERIVED status `executed`, and no `--rerun`' while leaving the sentence '`complete` is refused beside `executed` because ...' in place -> test PASSES (1 pass, 0 fail). Removing both -> FAILS. So the trigger half of D-04 is unpinned on its own.
gaps.missing: Assert the derived statuses against the refusal's TRIGGER clause (the text before `-> stop:`) rather than the whole arm, so a narrowed trigger reddens even when the rationale sentence still names `complete`.

human_checks.name: Run /cad-execute <N> against a phase whose DERIVED status is `executed` and observe the refusal, then run `node cadence-core/bin/planning.mjs trace render --phase <N>`
human_checks.expected: It stops in the locate step with the refusal naming /cad-undo <N> then /cad-execute <N> and --rerun; the trace shows no phase_start anchor and no executor dispatch for that invocation.
human_checks.why_human: Out of reach for this agent: the refusal is prose executed by the /cad-execute slash command in the user's own session, and a subagent cannot invoke a slash command or produce the trace append that would prove one did not happen. Static placement (locate at execute.md:8, ahead of git_guard at :58 and its phase_start append at :109) is already verified; only the firing is unobserved.

human_checks.name: Do a deliberate second run of one plan (/cad-execute <N> --rerun) and inspect <plandir>/reports/ plus git log for that plan afterwards
human_checks.expected: The first run's report is readable at plan-<k>.<n>.md with its original bytes, the second run's record is at plan-<k>.md, and both are in history after the docs commit (and, on the worktree path, after the executor's own report commit - which is the gap above).
human_checks.why_human: Irreversible against the real repo: the only artifact that performs the rename is a live cad-executor dispatch, which writes files and makes real commits on this branch. Nothing in the tree imports report-rotation.mjs at runtime, so no read-only probe can observe the rule being obeyed.
